title: YCB power drill from DSLR photos: resolution and several camera heights
question: Is the drill limited by the photos rather than the algorithm, and do more pixels per millimetre and more camera heights fix it?

data.source: YCB object and model set, 035_power_drill, berkeley_rgb_highres (DSLR N1-N5, 120 angles, 4272 x 2848) and berkeley_rgbd (NP1-NP5, 1280 x 1024); CC BY 4.0, Calli et al.
data.used_as_inputs: photos every 6 degrees (60 per camera) and each camera's lens intrinsics N*_rgb_K / N*_rgb_d only
data.not_used_as_inputs: supplied poses, rig extrinsics (H_*_from_NP5), dataset masks, depth, scanner mesh
data.five_camera_preparation: every camera undistorted with its own calibration into one common pinhole lens (largest focal length 3808.56 px, centred principal point)
data.masks: our own SAM 2.1 masks (--masks sam --sam-prompt-mask background --sam-candidates several); five-camera runs import the same own masks to skip recomputation
data.cameras: our own turntable solver with --turntable-region surface
data.evaluation_reference: Google 64k scan, posthoc only; aligned to each run's camera frame (1) by photo-consistency of the scan under our cameras, refined from (2) a proper-similarity trimmed ICP to the mesh; both reported

code_changes.turntable_working_size: --turntable-working-size N (default 2200): features and camera solve on photos scaled to that longest side; lens and observations scaled back. Photos up to 2200 px unchanged: cameras.json, sparse_points.npy and every scene file byte-identical to the previous binary (efbd600 front end, sha256 ba66c832...) on a 2136 x 1424 capture
code_changes.turntable_rings: --turntable-rings N: per-turn solve; turns with plausible rings joined by RANSAC similarity on linked points; other turns registered photo by photo (DLT and nearby-camera starts, Gauss-Newton with shrinking inlier bound) in rounds; one joint bundle adjustment. Cross-turn matches only between features that turn with the object. Per-turn ring gates; optical-axis miss against the viewing distance for multi-turn captures. SAM prompt box per turn. Photo limit 96 per turn (SAM and cleanup limits 1536)
code_changes.dense_gray_budget: whole grey photos kept until mask repair only while they take at most 2 GiB; otherwise canvas plus a quarter canvas. Byte-identical meshes on both paths (sha256 3e9e0143... at 2136 x 1424, 8330004e... at 4272 x 2848); full-size peak memory 3.9 -> 2.2 GB

results.run: NP3, 60 photos, 1280 x 1024, own cameras (current input)
N3, 60 photos, 4272 x 2848, own cameras through the working resolution

results.turn_5: own solution not a ring (radius spread 15 %); registered photo by photo in two rounds (47, 13)

controls.half_size_cameras_scaled_to_full_size: F1 0.6765/0.8821/0.9543 (photo fit of the half-size frame): the native full-size cameras give the same result

fusion_grid_on_identical_full_size_depth.note: F1 at 0.5 %; finer grids add noise and holes (genus 26 -> 68 -> 202) and no visible relief

controls.chuck_masks: SAM still drops the black chuck in some steep views; the dense mask repair restores it when other heights keep it in the hull (mask-repair sheet inspected)

sheet.content: scan (evaluation only, CC BY 4.0) and three reconstructions in the scan's frame from five fixed directions

checks: clippy -D warnings default, capi and sam-onnx
photo front end byte identity below the working size
dense byte identity on both grey-memory paths
limits: One object, one capture rig; the gain from resolution is expected wherever depth noise is at the photo limit, not shown on other objects here.
Surfaces remain mildly lumpy; vents, knurling and lettering (about 1 mm) are not recovered.
Scores depend on the scan alignment: the two fits differ by up to 0.08 F1 at 0.5 %.
Five-camera turns at 2 % precision are slightly below one turn's: the newly seen sides are noisier.

The six-object dense gate was not rerun: dense defaults are unchanged, and those captures (73 photos of 1749 x 1155, about 0.6 GB of grey) take the unchanged paths of the working resolution and grey budget; byte identity was verified on drill captures, not rerun on the six objects.
No browser execution of the multi-turn front end; 300 full-size photos need about 5.4 GB in the native dense stage.
